drug_class: GLP-1 receptor agonist (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist)
purpose: Dulaglutide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults and children (10 years and older) with type 2 diabetes. It is also used to lower the risk of serious heart problems like heart attack or stroke in people who have heart disease or are at high risk for it. It is not used for type 1 diabetes.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a hormone called GLP-1 after you eat, which tells your pancreas to release insulin and helps keep your blood sugar from going too high. Dulaglutide works like that natural hormone — it helps your pancreas release the right amount of insulin when your blood sugar is high, and it also slows down digestion so sugar enters your blood more slowly. This all works together to keep your blood sugar levels more steady throughout the day.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach pain, and decreased appetite. These are usually mild and often improve after the first few weeks as your body gets used to the medicine. Some people also notice burping or feeling full quickly.
warnings: This medication has a warning about a possible risk of thyroid tumors, including thyroid cancer, seen in animal studies — tell your doctor if you or a family member has ever had thyroid cancer or a condition called MEN 2. Do not use this medicine if you have a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma. Stop using it and call your doctor right away if you notice signs of pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to your back). It can also cause low blood sugar (especially if taken with other diabetes medicines), kidney problems, or serious allergic reactions.
typical_dosing: Dulaglutide comes as a pre-filled, easy-to-use injection pen that you inject under the skin (usually in your belly, thigh, or upper arm) once a week — on the same day each week. The usual starting dose is 0.75 mg once weekly. Your doctor may increase your dose to 1.5 mg, then up to 3 mg or 4.5 mg once weekly if needed for better blood sugar control. You can take it with or without food, and you can change the day of the week you use it as long as your doses are at least 3 days apart.
